name: Delia Derbyshire
hook: She turned a one-page score into the Doctor Who theme in 1963, note by note on tape, with no synthesizer and no keyboard.
blurb: Ron Grainer wrote the Doctor Who theme on paper. Delia Derbyshire, who joined the BBC Radiophonic Workshop in 1962, turned it into sound. There was no synthesizer. She recorded single notes from oscillators and a plucked string, changed their speed to change their pitch, and cut and joined the tape by hand. The bassline is a plucked string, and the swooping tune is oscillators. It was the first electronic theme tune on television, and it reached millions of homes a decade before synthesizers reached most bands. Grainer was credited as composer. The BBC did not put Workshop staff's names on screen, so it took decades for Derbyshire's name to be attached to the work. She left the BBC in 1973 and had mostly stopped making music by 1975. A large archive of her tapes, found after her death in 2001, has since changed how her work is understood.
